meta: Every phone brand used to have its own charger. AI and tools were the same: 5 AI apps and 10 tools meant 50 separate integrations. MCP, short for Model Context Protocol, is one shared port, like USB-C for AI.

muc.title: A different charger for every phone
muc.text: Back in the day, every phone brand had its own charger. You carried a bag of cables everywhere. AI and tools used to be exactly like that.

muc.title: Five AIs, ten tools
muc.text: Every AI app that wanted to connect to Drive, a calendar or sales software had to build a separate integration. Five AIs and ten tools means fifty integrations. One breaks, you fix one.

muc.title: One shared port
muc.text: MCP, short for Model Context Protocol, was made to solve that. It's a standard protocol, like a USB-C port for AI. Any tool with an MCP server can plug into any AI app that supports MCP.

muc.title: An open standard, owned by no one
muc.text: Anthropic, the company that makes Claude, released MCP in late 2024 as an open standard anyone can use. ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot then added support. MCP has now been handed to a shared industry group, so no single company owns it.

muc.title: Build once, use everywhere
muc.text: For you, the benefit is very practical: a tool builds an MCP server once, and it works in many AI apps. Switch to another AI, and your connections are still there.

muc.title: Count your sockets
muc.text: Open the connectors section in the AI app you use. Count how many tools are already connected. Many of them run on MCP.

muc.title: Inside the socket
muc.text: Plugging in is easy. But what's inside the socket? Part three opens it up.
